irrigation.source: General residential drip and spray design practice. Every number here is guidance, not a manufacturer's figure.

bed.plantFactorSource: Vegetable crops sit near the top of the MWELO plant-factor range for moderate-use plants; an estimate, unverified.

schedule.source: A typical residential schedule: deep and infrequent for established plants, early morning, valves one after another. Guidance only; not a controller program.
schedule.windowNote: Watering avoids 9 am to 4 pm, the hours many Southern California water agencies restrict.

prices.note: Stand-in prices for a rough idea only, not a quote.

conflicts.source: Design choices, not code requirements. Distances are adjustable here.

species.name: California towhee
species.note: Scratches in leaf litter under shrubs, all year.

species.name: Bushtit
species.note: Roams in chattering flocks through shrubs and trees, all year.

species.name: California scrub-jay
species.note: Raids fruit and acorns, all year.

species.name: Northern mockingbird
species.note: Eats fruit and berries, all year.

species.name: House finch
species.note: Perches in shrubs and trees, all year.

species.name: Cedar waxwing
species.note: Winter flocks that strip berries and fruit, November to April.

species.name: White-crowned sparrow
species.note: Winters here, feeding on the ground, October to April.

species.name: Yellow-rumped warbler
species.note: Winters here, hunting insects in shrubs and trees, October to April.

species.name: Black-headed grosbeak
species.note: A summer visitor that nests in trees, April to August.

species.name: Hooded oriole
species.note: A summer visitor that sips nectar from flowers, April to August.

water.source: A stand-in for what the water costs you: $10 per hundred cubic feet (748 gallons). For comparison, LADWP's July to December 2026 notice puts a typical single-dwelling 10 HCF monthly bill at $122.91 (about $12.29 an HCF with fixed charges), and its upper tiers cost more than its first; the notice's tier tables could not be read cleanly, so no tier rate is used. Replace it with the rate on your own bill.

reference.name: LADWP July to December 2026 biannual notice of change in water rates

pricing.source: Median retail container prices from public nursery price lists: Growing Works (Turning Point Foundation, Santa Barbara County, California) retail availability list, February 2026, for 1, 5 and 10/15 gallon (about 280 priced plants); 24 inch box from the public price pages of GDNC Nursery and Moosa Creek Nursery. Hardscape prices are still stand-ins.

references.name: Growing Works retail availability, February 2026 (Turning Point Foundation)
references.note: Median of every priced plant on the list: 1 gal $12 (quartiles 12 to 22, 183 plants), 2 gal $25, 5 gal $44 (quartiles 38 to 47, 283 plants), 10/15 gal $83 (quartiles 72 to 87, 283 plants). The list includes a clearance on succulents, which lowers the 1 gallon figures a little.

references.name: GDNC Nursery, general plant pricing
references.note: 24 inch box trees $200 to $250; 15 gallon $120 (desert trees, retail).

references.name: Moosa Creek Nursery wholesale availability
references.note: A 24 inch box tree $179.95 wholesale (San Diego County, California natives).

references.name: USDA NASS Census of Horticultural Specialties (2024)
references.note: National nursery stock sales by operation and container type; it reports dollars sold, not a price for each plant, so it is not used for the defaults.

anatomy.note: Shares of stature, general estimates: adult segment ratios after Drillis and Contini (1966); children's head and leg shares from growth studies; unverified against one source. A figure is the stature times these.
